variations: Missing Glove: tuck one of your worn gloves under a cushion across the room, and let your dog find it.
Easier: one coat only, with the pocket flap held open and the pouch just visible.
Seated or low-mobility: drape the coat over your own chair arm and stay in the chair.
Bigger: a three-coat line-up with two decoys, run over two evenings.
supplies: Two coats, one worn by you and one freshly washed
A little of today's regular food or a favorite toy
optionalSupplies: A phone for the after photo
substitutes: No pouch? Put the loot loose in the pocket instead.
No second coat? Use a scarf or sweater.
title: The Pocket Heist
clue: Someone is napping on the sofa, and the loot is in their coat.
reveal: You play the sleeping mark while your dog finds the loot in your coat pocket. A worn coat, a sealed pouch, a second decoy coat and a nose that knows exactly which is yours.
objective: Hide a sealed pouch of loot in your own worn coat beside a decoy coat, and let your dog find the right pocket.
instructions: Make the loot: a few pieces of today's ration in a small cloth pouch knotted shut, or a favorite toy. Check the pocket is empty of everything else.
Wear your coat for a few minutes first so it carries your scent. Hang it over a chair beside a decoy coat, a freshly washed one you have not worn, with the loot in your coat's pocket.
Sit or lie on the sofa and play the sleeping mark, eyes soft, with a slow breath. Your dog is free to come and go.
Let your dog investigate. If they sniff, nose or paw at the right coat, that is the heist. Do not point, peek or help.
When they have the pouch, let them take it to wherever they like. Wake slowly with a quiet stretch and a soft word, rather than a gasp.
Open the pouch for them if they want, then take the cloth away: the loot is theirs, not the pouch. Check the pocket is empty and put the coats away.
twist: You are the unwitting mark: your dog identifies your coat among two, using nothing but scent.
completion: Your dog has had a go at the coat and the loot is found or the dog has walked off, and either counts.
photoIdea: A relaxed photo of your dog with the opened pouch beside the coat, taken from the sofa.
memoryPrompt: Which coat did your dog choose, and how long did the mark stay asleep?
dietNotes: Use part of today's normal ration and count it in. Ask your vet if your dog has dietary restrictions, allergies or health conditions.
safety: Once the pouch is open, take the cloth away and never snatch the loot back or chase if they carry it off.
Run it one dog at a time, and skip the dramatic gasp if yours is easily startled.
Use only part of today's normal food, never chocolate, grapes, raisins or xylitol.
